key_terms.الْمَوْعُودِ: The promised, referring to that which was divinely promised
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ: The day, often referring to the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What does 'the promised day' refer to in Shia Islamic eschatology?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase underscores the certainty of the Ma'ad (Return), often linked with the concept of 'Alam al-Dharr' where the souls of the progeny of Adam testified to God's lordship. It serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is not merely a future event but a pre-ordained reality that validates divine justice and the eventual triumph of the Ahl al-Bayt.
